# Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming — facts

## Structure and components

- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that the degree of symptom responsiveness to levodopa should be assessed and considered but should not be the only criterion for candidacy; a 2020 selection review recommends the levodopa challenge test as a key presurgical tool, states that the rule of UPDRS part-III improvement greater than 30% should not be strictly applied, and notes that patients with disabling dopa-resistant tremor could represent an exception. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7761824/

## How it works

- [statement] When substantial dopaminergic medication reduction is the main surgical goal, evidence and the CNS guideline favor STN over GPi; medication reduction remains an individualized objective. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01015-x
- [statement] When medication reduction is not anticipated and suppressing on-medication dyskinesia is the goal, the CNS guideline favors GPi; GPi can have a direct antidyskinetic effect while medication is maintained. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] Complete withdrawal of dopaminergic medication after STN DBS is discouraged in the programming review because a hypodopaminergic state can cause apathy and depression, sometimes delayed for weeks; medication adjustment and stimulation adjustment should be coordinated. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] A 2020 selection review describes levodopa-resistant axial symptoms as a relative contraindication for surgery, while the 2026 referral consensus states that axial symptoms and freezing of gait should not be the sole indication for DBS but, when levodopa-responsive and associated with disabling motor fluctuations, may benefit from appropriately targeted and individualized DBS approaches and should not be viewed as absolute contraindications to surgery. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7761824/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3
- [statement] A programming review states that rigidity is typically used to judge the effect of STN-DBS because it does not fluctuate, responds to stimulation adjustments within seconds and does not depend on patient fatigue or cooperation, that no single clinical sign should be used alone to judge the therapeutic effect, and that the contact with the lowest threshold for beneficial effects and the widest therapeutic window is then selected for chronic stimulation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The 2026 expert consensus on referral for DBS states that patients with Parkinson's disease supported by the IPMDS clinical diagnostic criteria should be considered for DBS surgery evaluation in situations that include troublesome motor fluctuations and/or dyskinesia that interfere with functioning or quality of life despite optimal medical management, or disabling tremor that is refractory to an adequate levodopa trial. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5632902/
- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that pre-DBS assessments should include neurological, neurosurgical and neuropsychological evaluations and discussion of the patient's and family's goals and expectations, and that evaluation by an interdisciplinary team is the optimal approach for selecting DBS candidates; a review of patient and target selection adds that preoperative neuropsychiatric and neuropsychological assessment is necessary for risk stratification and that psychiatric clinical stability and social support should be determined before surgery. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01015-x
- [statement] For candidates with substantial concern about cognitive decline or depression, the CNS guideline advises considering GPi over STN while weighing the other goals of surgery; this is risk-based selection, not a guarantee of cognitive or mood safety. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that gait impairment, freezing of gait and imbalance should not be the primary indications for surgery, that the risk of potential worsening of balance should be discussed with patients pre-operatively, and that DBS is unlikely to improve speech and speech impairment is a potential side effect of stimulation. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] A 2025 review of DBS selection and programming states that programming begins once lead placement is confirmed and hardware integrity is ensured through an impedance check, that programming usually begins 3 to 4 weeks after lead implantation because microlesion effects can cause transient motor improvement, and that brief programming sessions can capture acute side effects but may fail to identify the full range of side effects that emerge with chronic stimulation. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01015-x · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] In the 36-month randomized-trial follow-up, quality-of-life gains diminished and cognitive measures declined despite maintained motor improvement; sustained motor benefit should not be equated with arresting disease progression. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3385495/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] The 2022 EAN/MDS-ES guideline on invasive therapies states that GPi-DBS can also be offered for advanced Parkinson's disease with fluctuations, that for early Parkinson's disease with early fluctuations STN-DBS is likely to improve motor symptoms and quality of life and can be offered, and that DBS should not be offered to people with early Parkinson's disease without fluctuations. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35791766/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Both STN and GPi are effective motor-symptom targets; the CNS guideline supports either target for motor treatment rather than a universal target preference. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] The randomized unilateral COMPARE trial reported no significant STN-versus-GPi difference in its co-primary mood and cognitive outcomes at optimal settings. It also reported adverse mood effects with ventral stimulation in both targets and greater letter-fluency deterioration in nonoptimal STN conditions; these setting-specific findings should not be generalized into inevitable global cognitive decline. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2692580/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that evidence exists that patients with cognitive impairment may still benefit from DBS for motor symptoms, that there is no data-driven cognitive-performance cut-off for considering DBS, and that mood, anxiety and other psychiatric disturbances do not necessarily exclude candidacy while significant psychiatric symptoms identified by the interdisciplinary team should be addressed prior to surgery. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] For conventional ring-contact programming, monopolar review tests contacts individually with the lead contact as cathode and pulse-generator case as anode, identifying benefit and adverse-effect thresholds to select a therapeutic window. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5632902/
- [statement] Conventional initial monopolar testing commonly holds pulse width at 60 μs and frequency at 130 Hz while amplitude is increased to identify benefit and side-effect thresholds. These are starting settings described in programming literature, not a universal prescription. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5925823/
- [statement] Two programming reviews describe a programming visit as including questions about symptom changes since the last visit, a clinical examination, and checks of lead type, electrode configuration, impedance and battery; one of them states that there are no validated and well-established programming protocols. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5632902/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5925823/
- [statement] For persistent stimulation-related adverse effects, the programming review recommends checking electrode location, reducing stimulation current and/or changing the active contact; alternative configurations can restrict current spread. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] Either STN or GPi can be selected for motor benefit; in the randomized trial’s 36-month follow-up, motor improvement was sustained and comparable between targets. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3385495/
